news.title: New Zealand U-17 men’s team visit Japan for World Cup preparation
news.lede: New Zealand’s U-17 men will begin an important phase of their FIFA World Cup preparations when they open a three-match tournament in Japan. Head coach Martin Bullock’s 18-player squad will face hosts Niigata, Myanmar and Japan at the International Youth Soccer Tournament in Niigata. The tournament provides New Zealand with competitive international football two months before the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup in Qatar. The squad prepared for Japan with two matches between academy teams from Wellington Phoenix and Auckland United at the NZCIS facility in Trentham last weekend.

news.title: World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente extends Spain contract to 2032
news.lede: Luis de la Fuente's new contract will extend his tenure as Spain head coach to 10 years. World Cup-winning head coach Luis de la Fuente has agreed a contract extension with Spain until 2032. The 65-year-old's previous deal was due to expire in 2028. De la Fuente, who guided Spain to their fourth European Championship title in 2024 before securing global honours this summer, is now set to remain in charge for Spain's World Cup defence on home soil in 2030.

news.title: FIFA moves to review Infantino’s shelved World Cup investment plan amid Infantino scrutiny
news.lede: September 16, 2026 Adejayan Gbenga Sports 0. FIFA has confirmed that a review of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise investment proposal will be presented to the FIFA Council amid growing criticism over the controversial plan. The development followed criticism from Danish Football Association president Jesper Moller, who accused FIFA of failing to provide answers to what he described as “critical questions” surrounding the shelved proposal. FIFA said the matter would be reviewed in accordance with its governance procedures, with the findings eventually presented to the FIFA Council.

news.title: USA exit U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism
news.lede: Brazil advance to quarter-finals in Poland. Americans have not won tournament since 2012. US youth teams have struggled in recent showings. The United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw after extra-time.

news.title: Tuchel: England was 'waiting for death' in World Cup semifinal defeat
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel said that England were "waiting for death" in their World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as the Three Lions boss mounted another defence of his controversial substitutions. Tuchel is preparing to name his squad for England's first matches since the painful end of their World Cup campaign. But, ahead of Nations League matches against Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic, he revealed that he is still haunted by the pain of their failed bid to reach a first World Cup final since 1966. England blew the lead given to them by Anthony Gordon as late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez sealed Argentina's 2-1 victory.

news.title: Tuchel: Substitution decisions in the match against Argentina at the World Cup are my scar
news.lede: England manager Thomas Tuchel has said that the controversial defensive changes he made in the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina are a scar on him and that he has to live with them. England lost 2-1 to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals in Atlanta on July 15. Tuchel's team took a 1-0 lead with five minutes remaining through Anthony Gordon's 55th-minute goal, but Argentina turned the game around with goals from Enzo Fernandez in the 85th and Lautaro Martinez in the second minute of stoppage time. Tuchel was heavily criticised for making defensive changes midway through the first half, switching to a five-man backline.

news.title: 'I have to live with it' - Thomas Tuchel admits tactical mistake cost England in World Cup heartbreak against Argentina
news.lede: THOMAS TUCHEL says he and his England side will always carry the “scars” of their World Cup near-miss. Speaking at length for the first time since the third-place finish in North America, the Three Lions chief conceded the 2-1 defeat against Argentina in Atlanta will always be a huge regret. Tuchel was widely criticised for his tactical negativity after Anthony Gordon put England ahead, as his side dropped back into a nine-man defensive line. Now the German, who said he had only watched “clips” of the match since the summer, revealed his feelings of frustration and disappointment but insisted he would not be “tortured” by the exit.
